To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prion like domain of the translation factor Sup35 promotes phase separation into protective gels during stress.
prion domains can drive reversible liquid liquid phase separation and gel formation in response to environmental stress, and that this function is shared by prion domains in distantly related yeast.

the prion like domain of Sup35 promotes the reversible liquid like phase separation of the essential translation termination Sup35 protein in response to stress and that this phase separation promotes cellular survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of intrinsically unfolded proteins in the cell.
the molecular mechanisms of prion like proteins.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that allow proteins to respond to stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prion like domains are stress sensors that modify protein phase behavior and promote cell survival in harsh environmental conditions.

the prion domains of the translation termination factors of budding yeast and f ission yeast are stress sensors that promote phase separation of the protein and thereby protect the essential translation factor from irreversible aggregation.
this paper demonstrates a new role for prion domains, namely as stress response elements that promote cell fitness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prion domains are a class of proteins that can be used by the cell to sense and respond quickly to environmental stress.
the prion domains of Sup35 and other prion domain proteins are protein specific sensors that respond to environmental changes by phase separation and gel formation.
prion like domains can be considered as a type of pH sensor that promotes phase separation and gel formation in cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phase separation is a common cellular mechanism for stress response.
the prion like domains are not just drivers of aggregation.
prion domains have an unexpected and conserved function as pH sensors that regulate phase separation.
